CA.blurb: Chaparral, oak woodland, coastal sage scrub and valley grassland. A summer-dormant, winter-growing flora: the cardinal rule is no summer irrigation once established.
CA.name: California Floristic Province

FL.blurb: Pine rockland, scrub, flatwoods and hardwood hammock. Bloom is nearly year-round, so designs emphasise evergreen structure and continuous nectar rather than one summer peak.
FL.epa_l1: Tropical Wet Forests / Eastern Temperate Forests
FL.name: Florida & Subtropical Gulf

GP.blurb: Mixed-grass and shortgrass prairie. Wind, cold and drought select for low, fine-textured, deeply taprooted plants; blue grama and little bluestem form the matrix.
GP.epa_l2: West-Central Semi-Arid Prairies, South Central Semi-Arid Prairies
GP.name: Great Plains

MTN.blurb: Sagebrush steppe, pinyon-juniper woodland and montane meadow. Intense sun, cold winters and lean alkaline soils; gravel-garden technique outperforms conventional beds.
MTN.epa_l1: North American Deserts / Northwestern Forested Mountains
MTN.name: Rocky Mountains & Intermountain West

MW.blurb: Tallgrass prairie, oak savanna and beech-maple forest. The richest palette in North America for sunny matrix planting: deep-rooted composites and warm-season bunchgrasses.
MW.epa_l2: Central USA Plains, Temperate Prairies, Mixed Wood Plains
MW.name: Midwest & Great Lakes

NE.blurb: Oak-hickory and northern hardwood forest, coastal plain and Appalachian uplands. Quercus, Prunus, Salix, Betula and Vaccinium are the keystone woody genera; Solidago and Symphyotrichum carry the late season.
NE.epa_l2: Mixed Wood Plains, Atlantic Highlands, Northeastern Coastal Zone
NE.name: Northeast & Mid-Atlantic

PNW.blurb: Douglas-fir and western hemlock forest with Willamette and Puget prairie remnants. Wet winters and dry summers: evergreen shade layers plus summer-dry meadow species.
PNW.name: Pacific Northwest (west of the Cascades)

SE.blurb: Longleaf pine savanna, oak-hickory-pine and bottomland hardwood. A fire-adapted grassland flora with exceptional late-summer and autumn bloom; heat and humidity tolerance is the limiting design factor.
SE.epa_l2: Southeastern USA Plains, Mississippi Alluvial & SE Coastal Plains, Ozark/Ouachita
SE.name: Southeast (Piedmont, Coastal Plain, Gulf)

SW.blurb: Sonoran, Chihuahuan and Mojave desert scrub. Design around evergreen structure, silver foliage and monsoon-timed bloom; irrigation beyond establishment usually kills these plants.
SW.epa_l2: Warm Deserts (Sonoran, Chihuahuan, Mojave), Southern Semi-Arid Highlands
SW.name: Southwest Deserts

TX.blurb: Limestone Hill Country, blackland prairie and coastal prairie. Alkaline soils and violent summer heat favour salvias, penstemons, daleas and muhly grasses.
TX.epa_l2: Edwards Plateau, Cross Timbers, Texas Blackland Prairies, Tamaulipan Plains
TX.name: Texas & South-Central
